messages.author: 2be20c634cab2dbb
messages.subject: Using Rhipe with RStudio Server
parts:
Hello,

I am able use Rhipe correctly in R in the command line using my linux
server. It is able to use the HDFS. I've run tests, and they all work.

However, I am trying to use RStudio Server to connect to my R
environment, via remote connection. Has anywone used RStudio Server
with Rhipe? It seems to be working, RStudio Server anyways; I'm able
to login and use the R environment on my remote server. It's when I
load the library(Rhipe) on the client side, using RStudio's web-
interface, that I run into problems.

It pulls up the warning:

Warning messages:
1: In onload.2(libname, pkgname) :
Rhipe requires the HADOOP or HADOOP_BIN environment variable to be
present
$HADOOP/bin/hadoop or $HADOOP_BIN/hadoop should exists
2: In onload.2(libname, pkgname) :
HADOOP_BIN is missing, using $HADOOP/bin

Afterwards, I type in rhinit(), and I get this:

/bin/hadoop jar /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/Rhipe/java/Rhipe.jar
org.godhuli.rhipe.PersonalServer localhost /tmp/RtmpWbI6Mj/
sockets32e81977 /tmp/RtmpWbI6Mj/signal1d0278a4 0
sh: /bin/hadoop: not found

Saying all this, I don't run into this problem using R directly on my
linux server, via command line. Rhipe works fine there, at least so
far running the tests.

Please let me know if anyone has had experience with RStudio Server,
or if there is any suggestions on other software to access Rhipe, via
a remote linux server.

I am using Ubuntu 10.10 (64bit), Apache Hadoop 0.20.2, RHIPE 0.65.4,
protobuf 2.3.0, R version 2.13.0, and Hive 0.7.1

Let me know if you need other information.

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Using Rhipe with RStudio Server
parts:
Issue this comman in your RStudio session

Sys.getenv(c("HADOOP","HADOOP_BIN"))

I issued that command; it made me remember that I had set HADOOP_HOME
but not HADOOP, so I did that--I've tried setting environmental
variables in ~/.profile and /etc/bash.bashrc. Either seems to work to
run everything correctly (Hadoop and Rhipe), except when I tried to
load Rhipe's library in Rstudio. Issuing the command in RStudio gave
me this (not good):
Sys.getenv(c("HADOOP","HADOOP_BIN"))

HADOOP HADOOP_BIN
"" ""

Instead of what I get when direct on the server:
Sys.getenv(c("HADOOP","HADOOP_BIN"))

HADOOP HADOOP_BIN
"/usr/local/hadoop" "/usr/local/hadoop/bin"


Still, everthing works running the library Rhipe directly on the
server.

Also, when I install Rhipe with the command: sudo R CMD INSTALL
Rhipe_0.65.4.tar.gz, I do get the warning messages, which is weird I
suppose:

installing to /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/Rhipe/libs
** R
** inst
** preparing package for lazy loading
** help
*** installing help indices
** building package indices ...
** testing if installed package can be loaded
--------------------------------------------------------
| IMPORTANT: Before using Rhipe call rhinit() |
| Rhipe will not work or most probably crash |
--------------------------------------------------------

Warning messages:
1: In onload.2(libname, pkgname) :
Rhipe requires the HADOOP or HADOOP_BIN environment variable to be
present
$HADOOP/bin/hadoop or $HADOOP_BIN/hadoop should exists
2: In onload.2(libname, pkgname) :
HADOOP_BIN is missing, using $HADOOP/bin

* DONE (Rhipe)

----->

This is because when I load the library Rhipe in R (directly through
the linux server), I don't get these warning messages, just this:

> library(Rhipe)
--------------------------------------------------------
| IMPORTANT: Before using Rhipe call rhinit() |
| Rhipe will not work or most probably crash |
--------------------------------------------------------
> rhinit(TRUE, TRUE)
/usr/local/hadoop/bin/hadoop jar /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/Rhipe/
java/Rhipe.jar org.godhuli.rhipe.PersonalServer localhost /tmp/
Rtmpl6UfB8/socketsad9a8d4 /tmp/Rtmpl6UfB8/signal99aaad9 0
Rhipe initialization complete
Rhipe first run complete
[1] TRUE

Are those warning messages just default when you install the Rhipe add-
on?

Thank you for the assistance! I'm hoping you know somewhere to look
next. The team I'm working on really wants an interface to use R and
Hadoop (e.g., Rhipe) on the client side. This would be great to get to
work!

I guess it could be an issue with RStudio. Has anyone ever used it, or
if so, have you used it with the Rhipe add-on?

Okay here.


There are other things to be worried here. I'm not sure how Rstudio
works, when a user logs in
is a new session started i.e. does each user get their own session?
Then if Rhipe is loaded, each user
will get their own Rhipe server running in the background (a good
thing) - but launched as which user? the rstudio user?
or the user logged in.

if environment variables are an issue, just set them before loading
Rhipe. It's not nice, but Rhipe really does need those
environment variables to locate the hadoop configuration files.

Cheers
Saptarshi

parts:
It's the end of the day for me, but by setting the environmental
variables in R, through RStudio, this method did work. I never tried
that before. I guess I should have. Honestly, I'm just an intern and
am not the best programmer so stuff slips by me. Thanks for the hint!
It now works through RStudio.

However, like you say this isn't that nice, but it will do (I can just
create a script to initiate these commands at the begining of the
session anyways).

What do you mean by: "does restarting rstudio pick up these
envrionment variables"? If you mean initiating the command sudo
rstudio-server restart, this does nothing to alleviate the problem. I
think it just happens to be an issue with RStudio. I think it's in
beta anyways.

Concerning logging in to RStudio, it does save the session if I log in
and out on the same user. I'm guessing each user gets their own
session but that's about it. I'll have to look into that possibly next
week. Are you saying could have something to do with the environmental
variable problem on the RStudio side?

Thank you for the help, at least I got it to work. I'll try and send
an update next week.
